public_rationale: The searched records do not measure the asserted funding share. Investment totals identify recipients or sectors, while the more detailed compute analysis covers particular companies and different spending categories. It cannot establish what fraction of all AI funding pursued LLM enlargement. The available evidence therefore neither supports nor decisively contradicts nearly all.
limitations: The selected annual period cannot settle an unspecified cumulative historical claim.
The retrospective compute analysis was published after the post but before the evaluation cutoff.
No numerical threshold or accounting basis can fairly be supplied on the speaker's behalf.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nearly all AI funding has gone to making LLMs larger.

statement.excerpt: Yet nearly all funding has been aimed simply at making them larger.
statement.document_title: How o3 and Grok 4 Accidentally Vindicated Neurosymbolic AI

from_speaker: aimed simply at making them larger
our_interpretation: Them refers to LLMs. The ordinary reading is an overwhelming share of AI funding directed solely toward increasing LLM scale.
Funding a company that develops LLMs does not establish that its money was devoted solely to larger models.
Use calendar 2024 as the latest complete annual funding period publicly reportable before the post. The alternative cumulative reading has no specified starting date.
This is an aggregate sector allocation claim, not a financial figure for a named company; metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable funding and allocation records show that an overwhelming share of AI funding was directed solely toward increasing LLM size or pretraining scale.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish that a substantial share of the same funding total was allocated to other purposes.

evidence.locator: Opening discussion following the estimate of OpenAI's 2024 compute allocation
evidence.explanation: Epoch estimates that roughly $500 million of OpenAI's approximately $5 billion in 2024 R&D compute went to final training runs. This challenges equating all compute expenditure with final training, but experiments and other research may also pursue scale, and one company's compute spending does not measure all AI funding.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defined funding universe and comparable allocation records separating LLM enlargement from other purposes, with enough coverage to determine whether the former overwhelmingly dominated.
